NEWS RELEASE
TSX: ELD NYSE: EGO October 28, 2026

Eldorado Gold Reports Q3 2026 Financial and Operational Results and Updates 2026 Guidance; Skouries and McIlvenna Bay Advancing Toward Commercial Production (All amounts expressed in U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted) VANCOUVER, BC - Eldorado Gold Corporation (“Eldorado”, "Eldorado Gold" or “the Company”) today reports the Company’s financial and operational results for the third quarter of 2026. For further information, please see the Company’s Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A") filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.com under the Company’s profile. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights Operations •Gold production: 106,351 ounces. •Gold sales: 107,164 ounces at an average realized gold price per ounce sold(1) of $4,326. •Total cash costs(1): $1,415 per ounce sold. •All-in sustaining costs ("AISC")(1): $2,050 per ounce sold. •Total capital expenditures: $452.3 million, including $108.6 million of project capital and $84.3 million of accelerated operational capital at Skouries, and $87.5 million project capital invested at McIlvenna Bay. Growth capital(1) at the operating mines totalled $105.1 million and sustaining capital(1) at the operating mines totalled $52.1 million. Financial •Revenue: $511.9 million. •Production costs: $199.8 million. •Net cash generated from operating activities from continuing operations: $134.8 million. •Cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital(1): $248.8 million. •Cash and cash equivalents: $396.8 million as at September 30, 2026, excluding $71.9 million of restricted cash designated for Skouries Term Facility(2) loan repayments. •Net earnings attributable to shareholders: $118.0 million, or $0.45 basic earnings per share. •Adjusted net earnings(1): $127.0 million or $0.49 per share in Q3 2026. Adjustments in Q3 2026 include a $7.4 million loss on foreign exchange translation of deferred tax balances and a $4.0 million unrealized gain on derivative instruments. •Adjusted net earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA")(1): $275.2 million in Q3 2026. •Free cash flow(1): Consolidated free cash flow was negative $191.1 million in Q3 2026, reflecting the significant level of investment in Skouries and McIlvenna Bay as both operations advance toward commercial production. For additional context free cash flow excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay(1) was $98.3 million. (1) These financial measures or ratios are non-IFRS financial measures or ratios. (2) The Skouries Term Facility is defined as the Commercial Loan Facility, the RRF Facility and the Contingent Overrun Facility ("Term Facility").

Production and Cost Outlook Production Guidance Based on year-to-date performance through the third quarter, Eldorado has revised its 2026 production outlook for its operating assets, excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, to 410,000 to 430,000 ounces of gold, compared with original guidance of 430,000 to 490,000 ounces. The revised 2026 production outlook, including Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, is 425,000 to 475,000 ounces of gold, compared with original guidance of 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. Strong performance at Lamaque, supported by increasing contributions from high-grade Ormaque ore, is partially offsetting lower expected production at Kisladag and Olympias as well as the impact of a slower than expected ramp-up at Skouries. •Lamaque – Strong operating execution and increasing contributions from high-grade Ormaque ore continue to support strong production performance. Ormaque is becoming an increasingly important source of high-grade ore for Lamaque. •Kisladag – Lower production for 2026 primarily reflects lower-grade ore associated with the current mining sequence and slower than planned mining progress during the third quarter, which delayed access to higher-grade material. Higher-grade material is now being stacked on the North Heap Leach Pad; however, given the approximately 300-day leach cycle, the associated production benefit is expected toward the end of the fourth quarter and into 2027. •Olympias – Lower production for 2026 primarily reflects the timing of the 650 ktpa expansion, which reduces expected fourth-quarter throughput and production. The targeted 650 ktpa nameplate throughput rate is expected to be achieved in the first half of 2027. In addition, material with elevated lead and zinc content that was expected to be processed during the third quarter was instead stockpiled. This material is expected to be introduced through a controlled blending program during the fourth quarter to maintain stable plant performance and optimize recoveries. •Skouries – Gold production guidance for 2026 has been revised to 10,000 to 35,000 ounces, compared with prior guidance of 60,000 to 100,000 ounces, reflecting a slower-than-expected ramp-up. The revision reflects the timing of the ramp-up and does not change the Company’s expectations for Skouries’ longer-term design capacity with commercial production expected in late Q4 2026. •McIlvenna Bay – Gold production continues to track within the 5,000 to 10,000 ounce guidance range for 2026. Commercial production is expected in late Q4 2026. Base metal production ranges, including Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, have also been revised primarily reflecting the slower-than-expected ramp-up at Skouries, and lower production at Olympias: •Copper production: 10 to 25 million pounds (previously 20 to 40 million pounds) •Silver production: 1.2 to 1.5 million ounces (previously 1.55 to 1.75 million ounces) •Lead production: 11 to 14 thousand tonnes (previously 15 to 18 thousand tonnes) •Zinc production: 14

to 20 thousand tonnes (previously 16 to 19 thousand tonnes) Cost Guidance Consolidated total cash cost guidance for operating assets, excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, has been revised to $1,400 to $1,500 per ounce sold, compared with original guidance of $1,220 to $1,420 per ounce sold. AISC guidance has been revised to $1,975 to $2,125 per ounce sold, compared to original guidance of $1,670 to $1,870 per ounce sold. The revisions primarily reflect: •Higher sustaining capital expenditures, including the earlier transition of Ormaque underground development at Lamaque from growth capital to sustaining capital following the earlier-than-expected receipt of the permit and advancement of development activities, as well as higher sustaining capital requirements at Olympias. •Lower production at Kisladag and Olympias, partially offset by higher production at Lamaque. •Higher royalty expense driven by higher realized metal prices. Capital Guidance •Sustaining capital – Guidance for operating assets, excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, has been revised to $170 to $190 million, compared with prior guidance of $140 to $165 million, primarily reflecting the earlier transition of Ormaque underground development at Lamaque from growth capital to sustaining capital and higher sustaining capital at Olympias due to increased filtration maintenance costs and additional contract support to advance access to higher grade underground zones.

•Growth capital – Guidance for operating assets, excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, has been revised to $395 to $430 million, compared with prior guidance of $375 to $405 million, primarily reflecting additional investment at Kisladag, including land acquisitions and increased waste movement for the Western Area, and higher capital requirements associated with the 650 ktpa expansion at Olympias. These increases are partially offset by lower growth capital at Lamaque following the earlier transition of Ormaque underground development to sustaining capital. Skouries – With commercial production expected in late Q4, total project capital for Skouries is estimated at approximately $1.425 billion, an increase that consists of $65 million of projects costs and $45 million of previously guided growth capital that had been expected following commercial production but is now expected to be incurred prior to commercial production and is therefore reported as project capital. The increase primarily reflects higher contractor requirements to complete construction and commissioning activities, the extended use of temporary generator sets prior to connection to permanent grid power, additional owner’s costs and other project execution-related costs associated with the longer commissioning period. Accelerated operational capital is expected to total $390 million, an increase that consists of $95 million of additional operational costs and $35 million of previously guided sustaining capital that had been expected following commercial production. It is now expected to be incurred and capitalized during the pre-commercial production period and is therefore reported as accelerated operating capital. This increase is separate from the increase in project capital. Up to an additional $30 million may be incurred, depending on the exact timing of commercial production. The classification of these expenditures will depend on when commercial production is achieved, with amounts potentially reflected in project capital, AOC, sustaining capital or growth capital. McIlvenna Bay – The total project capital cost estimate from June 1, 2024 to commercial production is expected to be $975 million, an increase of approximately $23 million following a slower than expected ramp-up toward commercial production. For 2026, growth capital post commercial production is expected to be approximately $15 million and sustaining capital post commercial production is expected to be $10 million. Depreciation Expense Guidance Depreciation expense guidance, for operating assets excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, has been reduced to $225 to $235 million, compared to prior guidance of $240 to $260 million, largely due to lower production. Depreciation expense at Skouries is not expected to be significant, compared with prior guidance of $15 to $35 million, as commercial production is expected in late Q4 2026. Corporate •On August 12, 2026 the Company amended the senior secured credit

facility, increasing total availability to $600 million, extending the maturity to March 1, 2029 and improving financial flexibility. •George Burns retired as Chief Executive Officer of Eldorado Gold, effective September 30, 2026. Following his retirement from management, Mr. Burns will remain on the Company’s Board of Directors. •Christian Milau assumed the role of President and Chief Executive Officer and joined the Board of Directors, effective September 30, 2026. •Paul Ferneyhough’s role expanded to Executive Vice President, Strategy and Chief Financial Officer, effective September 30, 2026. •Carissa Browning stepped down from the Board of Directors effective September 4, 2026. •On October 28, 2026, the Company declared a fourth quarter dividend of $0.075 per common share, payable on December 15, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 1, 2026.

Commentary “The third quarter marked an important step forward for Eldorado. Skouries produced first copper-gold concentrate and McIlvenna Bay continued to ramp up following first copper and zinc concentrate. At Skouries, the ramp-up has taken longer and cost more than we expected, and it is important that we acknowledge that directly,” said Christian Milau, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Our focus is on safely completing the remaining commissioning work, achieving commercial production and establishing stable, predictable operating performance. “As I begin my tenure as CEO, my focus is on building on Eldorado’s high-quality, long-life asset base and the investments already made, while improving execution consistency, enhancing capital discipline and converting those investments into stronger cash flow and per-share value. Shareholders should expect us to set clear expectations, report transparently on our progress and remain disciplined in how we allocate capital. “Beyond the near-term ramp-ups, we have substantial opportunity within the portfolio. Our focus is on maximizing the value of the assets we already own, maintaining balance-sheet strength and financial flexibility, and investing where expected returns justify the capital. As the new operations ramp up and generate increasing cash flow, we expect to have greater flexibility to balance debt reduction, reinvestment and shareholder returns. With Skouries and McIlvenna Bay advancing through commissioning and ramp-up, our priority is to execute the remaining work and translate the cash flow potential of these investments into stronger, sustainable cash generation and per-share value.”

Skouries Highlights The Skouries mine, part of the Kassandra Mines Complex, is located within the Halkidiki Peninsula of Northern Greece and is a high-grade copper-gold mine. In January 2022, Eldorado published the results of the Skouries Project Feasibility Study with a 20-year mine life and expected average annual production over the life of the mine of 140,000 ounces of gold and 67 million pounds of copper, or approximately 240,000 gold equivalent ounces(3). First production of the copper-gold concentrate was achieved on September 8, 2026, and commercial production is expected late in Q4 2026. Expected 2026 gold production was revised to between 10,000 and 35,000 ounces and copper production projected to be between 5 and 15 million pounds. Skouries site layout Concentrate Off-Take Agreements The Company has secured concentrate agreements with multiple offtakers for all anticipated Skouries production volumes for the next two years, with additional counterparty agreements in process covering production through to 2029. Market conditions for copper-gold concentrate remain highly competitive. Capital Estimate and Schedule With commercial production expected in late Q4, total project capital for Skouries is estimated at approximately $1.425 billion, an increase that consists of $65 million of projects costs and $45 million of previously guided growth capital that had been expected following commercial production but is now expected to be incurred prior to commercial production and is therefore reported as project capital. The increase primarily reflects higher contractor requirements to complete construction and commissioning activities, the extended use of temporary generator sets prior to connection to permanent grid power, additional owner’s costs and other project execution-related costs associated with the longer commissioning period. Accelerated operational capital is expected to total $390 million, an increase that consists of $95 million of additional operational costs and $35 million of previously guided sustaining capital that had been expected following commercial production. It is now expected to be incurred and capitalized during the pre-commercial production period and is therefore reported as accelerated operating capital. This increase is separate from the increase in project capital. Up to an additional $30 million may be incurred, depending on the exact timing of commercial production. The classification of these expenditures will depend on when commercial production is achieved, with amounts potentially reflected in project capital, AOC, sustaining capital or growth capital. Filtered Tailings Facility Commissioning of the filtered tailings facility continues to progress with two of the six filter presses operational. With these filter presses online, the plant is operating continuously and progressively increasing throughput as commissioning advances and the remaining filter presses are brought online. Commissioning of the remaining four filter presses is expected to be completed in November 2026. Integrated Extractive Waste Management Facility The initial filtered tailings placement areas are well advanced. The platform for the tailings stacker is complete and ready for assembly, while the access ramp and platform for the mobile (grasshopper) conveyors have been excavated and prepared for placement of the conveyor units. Construction of the rock buttress supporting the downstream embankment of the first filtered tailings placement area in the Karatza Lakkos ("KL") valley is progressing and will be completed ahead of tailings placement. Foundation preparation for the first phase of the KL filtered tailings embankment is substantially complete, and placement of engineered fill is underway across the full footprint. Construction of the low-grade ore stockpile continued advancing. The lower section has been completed and construction is now focusing on the upper section. Open Pit Mining The open pit mine is feeding the crusher from both the stockpile and directly from the open pit. At the end of Q3 2026, the stockpiles contained approximately 4.8 million tonnes of open pit and underground ore, representing an estimated 176,000 ounces of gold and 61 million pounds of copper. Underground Development The underground mine delivered 179 kt of ore to stockpiles during Q3 2026. Underground development continued according to plan, with a total of 2,101 metres of development during the quarter. The east ramp breakthrough to the underground works was achieved during the quarter and both ramps are now providing access in and out of the underground. Workforce As at September 30, 2026, there were approximately 2,297 personnel working on site, including 622 Skouries employees.

McIlvenna Bay Highlights The McIlvenna Bay mine, located in Saskatchewan, Canada, is a copper-zinc-gold-silver mine that Eldorado acquired through its acquisition of Foran, which closed on April 14, 2026. In March 2025, Foran published a McIlvenna Bay Project Feasibility Study, with an 18-year mine life and expected average annual production over the life of the mine of 41 million pounds of copper, 20,000 ounces of gold, 444,000 ounces of silver and 54 million pounds of zinc. First production of copper concentrate from McIlvenna Bay was achieved in June 2026 with production of first zinc concentrate achieved in July. The focus is now on optimizing operations and increasing throughput to full design capacity. The crushing, grinding and flotation circuits have been commissioned and are demonstrating increasing throughput as ramp-up progresses. Remaining ramp-up activities are focused primarily on solid-liquid separation in the pyrite and tailings thickeners, reagent control, and improving filtration rates and filter availability. Work in these areas continues to advance, with commercial production expected in late Q4 2026. The mine is expected to have a long life and is supported by a robust resource base, with highly prospective exploration upside across the broader district, including the nearby Tesla Zone. The inaugural Inferred Mineral Resource for Tesla is expected to be included in our annual Mineral Reserve and Mineral Resource update in the fourth quarter of 2026. Based on the prospectivity of the resource, we have initiated studies to evaluate material handling options for the mine, in addition to the mill expansion study that is underway, with resource conversion drilling planned for the Tesla resource. Once studies and conversion drilling have been advanced, we would expect to update the McIlvenna Bay Technical Report. Located in one of the world’s most attractive mining jurisdictions, the mine benefits from established infrastructure and is designated by the Government of Canada as a project of national significance to support critical mineral development.

Primary Crusher Building More than 400 kt of ore is available on surface for processing. The primary crusher is operating at design capacity, material transfer to the fine ore bin is as expected, and metal separation practices for underground material continue on surface. Process Plant The SAG and ball mill circuits continue to demonstrate increasing throughput as commissioning advances. As expected for a new processing plant, we continue to work through equipment, instrumentation and other availability-related challenges associated with ramp-up. Throughput is expected to continue increasing through the fourth quarter as the operation progresses toward commercial production.

SAG and Ball Mills Flotation All flotation circuits are fully commissioned and have successfully produced copper, zinc and pyrite concentrates. The regrind circuit is operational and supporting further improvements in concentrate quality as ramp-up progresses. Thickening & Filtration The thickening and filtration circuits are key to the ramp-up of production. The key operational focus is on reagent addition and thickener control which has impacted the solid-liquid separation quality and downstream process water clarity. The teams are working to optimize the thickener and filtration processes for long-term stability. Underground Development Underground development continues to advance well. In addition to the 409 kt of ore stockpiled on surface, the mine has approximately 63 kt of blasted inventory, more than 400 kt drilled off, and approximately 2.0 Mt of fully developed reserves within Block 1 and Block 2. Study Commenced on Processing Expansion, Including Throughput Increase and Silver-Lead Circuit The expansion study is underway to evaluate an increase in processing throughput and the incorporation of a silver‑lead circuit. The expansion will evaluate a potential increase of processing capacity at McIlvenna Bay from 4,900 tonnes per day to approximately 7,000 tonnes per day. The addition of a dedicated silver‑lead circuit into the flowsheet is expected to enable recovery of lead into a separate concentrate and improve payable silver recoveries relative to the current design. This initial study will assess the technical, economic, environmental and permitting considerations associated with the expansion. Any future development would be subject to completion of the project evaluation, receipt of required permits, Indigenous and Stakeholder engagement, and a positive final investment decision. The Company is targeting commissioning of the silver‑lead circuit in 2028 and the expansion in 2030. Positioned as the Foundation for Long-Term District Growth The McIlvenna Bay mine is core to our view of the district-scale geological potential to deliver future satellite development opportunities. Ongoing exploration will target additional resources, which could support further expansion or a separate processing facility over time. The 2026 exploration program includes approximately 14,000 metres of diamond drilling focused on resource expansion, high-grade extensions, and advancing regional targets. In parallel, core scanning programs will enhance geological modelling and orebody characterization. Airborne and ground geophysical surveys are expected to help refine known deposit footprints and identify new targets across the broader land package.

In Q3 2026, we produced 106,351 ounces of gold, a decrease from Q3 2025 production of 115,190 ounces. The decrease was driven by decreases at Kisladag, due to the planned lower ore grade stacked, and at Efemcukuru, due to lower ore grade, partially offset by higher production at Lamaque as a result of higher throughput, grade and recoveries, which includes the positive impact of Ormaque ore grades and improving productivity. Gold sales in Q3 2026 were 107,164 ounces, a decrease from 116,529 ounces sold in Q3 2025. The lower sales volume reflects lower production at Kisladag and Efemcukuru, partially offset by higher production at Lamaque. The average realized gold price was $4,326 per ounce sold in Q3 2026, an increase from $3,527 per ounce sold in Q3 2025. Total revenue increased to $511.9 million in Q3 2026 from $434.7 million in Q3 2025 and to $1,531.7 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from $1,241.7 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases in both periods were due to the higher average realized gold price, partially offset by lower volumes sold.

Production costs increased to $199.8 million in Q3 2026 from $164.1 million in Q3 2025 and to $572.8 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $474.6 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Increases in both periods were driven by higher royalties and the inclusion of pre-commercial production costs at McIlvenna Bay, together which accounted for approximately 32% and 45% of the increase to production costs for Q3 2026 and the nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. The remainder relates primarily to increases at Lamaque, due to increased volumes produced, higher maintenance costs and deepening the production centre of the Triangle Mine, and at Olympias due to higher labour, contractor and materials costs as well as higher volumes sold. Production costs include royalty expense, which increased to $31.8 million in Q3 2026 from $28.8 million in Q3 2025 and increased to $115.7 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $79.6 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Increases in both periods were due to higher average realized gold prices and higher royalty rates, partially offset by lower volumes sold. Total cash costs(5) averaged $1,415 per ounce sold in Q3 2026, an increase from $1,195 in Q3 2025, and $1,438 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $1,134 in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases in both the three and nine-month periods were primarily due to higher production costs and lower volumes sold, partially offset by higher costs allocated to by-products. AISC per ounce sold(5) averaged $2,050 in Q3 2026, an increase from $1,679 in Q3 2025, and $1,974 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $1,583 in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases in both periods were driven by higher total cash costs, higher sustaining capital expenditures and lower volumes sold. The Company reported net earnings attributable to shareholders from continuing operations of $118.0 million ($0.45 earnings per share) in Q3 2026 compared to net earnings of $56.5 million ($0.28 earnings per share) in Q3 2025 and net earnings of $427.2 million ($1.80 earnings per share) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to net earnings of $267.5 million ($1.31 earnings per share) in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net earnings in both periods were driven by higher average realized gold prices, foreign exchange gains and lower depreciation, partially offset by lower volumes sold, higher production costs and higher income tax expense. Adjusted net earnings(5) was $127.0 million ($0.49 adjusted earnings per share) in Q3 2026 compared to adjusted net earnings of $82.3 million ($0.41 adjusted earnings per share) in Q3 2025. Adjustments of non-recurring items in Q3 2026 include a $7.4 million loss on foreign exchange translation of deferred tax balances and a $4.0 million unrealized gain on derivative instruments. Kisladag Kisladag produced 22,713 ounces of gold in Q3 2026 compared to 37,184 ounces in Q3 2025, with the decrease due to lower planned grades associated with the current cutback and slower-than-planned mining progress, which delayed access to higher-grade material during the third quarter. Ore grade decreased to 0.55 grams per tonne in Q3 2026 from 0.70 grams per tonne in Q3 2025, partially offset by higher stacked tonnage, resulting in lower recoverable ounces during the quarter. Revenue decreased to $93.1 million in Q3 2026 from $130.5 million in Q3 2025, reflecting a decrease in gold ounces sold that was partially offset by the higher average realized gold price. Production costs increased to $51.1 million in Q3 2026 from $50.1 million in Q3 2025, driven by higher labour and contractor costs, higher maintenance and higher reagent costs for water management, offset by lower gold sales and lower royalty costs. Lower gold production and higher production costs were primarily responsible for the increase in total cash costs per ounce sold to $2,328 in Q3 2026 from $1,309 in Q3 2025. AISC per ounce sold increased to $2,832 in Q3 2026 from $1,545 in Q3 2025, primarily due to higher cash costs per ounce sold and higher sustaining costs. Sustaining capital expenditures were $9.2 million in Q3 2026 and $18.3 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which primarily included a new 300 tonne haul truck purchase, planned equipment rebuilds (including primary crusher refurbishment), interlifts for the leach pad and geotechnical drilling. Growth capital investment of $38.9 million and $122.7 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to waste stripping and associated equipment costs, continued construction of the North Heap Leach Pad ("NHLP") Phase 3, construction of the whole-ore agglomeration circuit and upgrades to the secondary crusher. Growth capital in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, also included one-time land purchases totalling $23.9 million required for the construction of the NHLP and North Rock Dump. Kisladag incurred higher reagent costs as a result of increased water management activities, predominantly in the second quarter following a period of higher‑than‑average precipitation in the first half of 2026, that resulted in elevated water levels within site ponds. The Company continues to actively manage water balances across the operation, with a focus on continuing to maximize on‑site water capture and reuse in support of its sustainability objectives, and has constructed additional water storage capacity to enhance operational flexibility. The Company continues to evaluate a pit shell based on gold price sensitivity analysis, which is expected to support further expansion into the western area of the pit and support resource expansion. New geological and metallurgical information will be incorporated into the life-of-mine optimization that will form part of the Mineral Reserve and

Mineral Resource update expected in Q4 2026. As part of this optimization work, the Company expects to evaluate an investment decision on additional screening before year-end. Progress on construction of the whole ore agglomeration circuit, which is configured to increase permeability and reduce leach time, is on track with earthworks well underway and all long-lead items procured. Commissioning and ramp-up are expected in H1 2027. Overall, this mine optimization plan is expected to support improved sequencing of ore and waste movement, and with implementation of whole ore agglomeration, is expected to contribute to more consistent year‑over‑year operating performance and higher production over the longer term.
